title: Ceratitis
text:
Described by Macleay in 1829.
Tribe: Ceratitidini | Species: ~80–100

title: Ceratitis
text:
Common name: Mediterranean fruit fly (Medfly)
Economic importance: One of the world’s most polyphagous pests, infesting over 300 host species. Established on every inhabited continent except Asia. Managed primarily through the Sterile Insect Technique (SIT).

title: Bactrocera
text:
Described by Macquart in 1835. Primarily Indo-Pacific in distribution, with several species now established as invasive pests in Africa, Europe, and the Americas.
Tribe: Dacini | Species: ~600

title: Bactrocera
text:
1 Bactrocera dorsalis (Hendel, 1912)
Common name: Oriental fruit fly
Economic importance: Major invasive pest of mango, guava, papaya, and hundreds of other hosts. Established in Africa after 2003.

title: Tephritidae Research Database
text: This database covers empirical research on Tephritid fruit flies (family Tephritidae), organised by genus and species. Each page shows active research themes, recent papers, and the researchers currently in this work. This page currently shows papers from 2026.

title: Tephritidae Research Database
text:
2 About
Papers are sourced from Google Scholar, PubMed, and Web of Science. Only empirical research papers are included — reviews are excluded unless otherwise noted. Coverage is currently limited to 2026 publications and will be extended retrospectively.

For questions or contributions contact: katie.millar@uea.ac.uk
